output.brief: The October night premium shortfalls came from one rule change, not from Fenmarch's data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a template to the night premium rule (NSP-02). It moved the start of the night window from 20:00 to 22:00. The change log called it a label correction with no effect on pay. The platform's tamper-proof audit trail shows otherwise. The collective agreement and the design document both say 20:00. An internal audit recalculation found 147 of 158 night workers underpaid. Each shortfall equals the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours, to the penny. Staff on 22:00–06:00 rosters were paid correctly. Re-running October in the test tenant with the window set back to 20:00 matched expected pay for all 158. Ardentra's data explanation doesn't hold up. Flagged records were underpaid at about the same rate as unflagged ones. Don't suspend the HR team and don't reload the data. Don't roll back release 7.4. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and verify it in the test tenant before 24 Nov. Then pay all underpaid staff, including the 8 who never raised a ticket, in an off-cycle payment. Revisit the clause 14.3 cost position, since the defect was Ardentra's. The fall in overtime cover may be partly due to the rota trial. That cause is still unsettled, so look at it separately before pausing the trial. I'm confident in the main finding.
